name: wan-s2-bulk
description: Plan 11.3's bulk half on kcptun's own defaults (S2: aes, fast, FEC 10/3, comp, sndwnd 128 / rcvwnd 512), over the same real path as wan-s1-bulk and with the same shape. S2 is the window-limited case: at 95 ms a 128-packet send window is about 15 Mbit/s whatever the link does, so this is where the FEC counters and the window behaviour are compared rather than the raw ceiling. Ports: the tunnel is 29910+ and the pingpong target 22700, not the 29900/22600 defaults, so a WAN run cannot collide with a netns lab that is up on either host — the port check unions the host's listeners with both lab namespaces', and a detached soak owns the defaults inside kr-srv. The iperf3 bitrate cap (400 Mbit/s) is a guard rail, not the measurement: it is well above what a 1-vCPU box drives through a tunnel at this RTT, so it does not bind, but it stops an unexpectedly fast path from saturating lab-arm64's NIC (tools/lab/README.md, safety rule 6). A cap that binds makes every implementation report the cap, which is how the first attempt at this rung wasted half an hour: 60 Mbit/s, 60 Mbit/s, both directions, both implementations. Measured on the 131 ms rung before the campaign: a Go client on one vCPU drove 200 Mbit/s up (cap-bound) and 145 Mbit/s down at a load average of 0.93, so the real limit is the client's single core, not the path — the cap is set above that so it never becomes the thing being compared. The reverse test starts 95 s after the forward one, not 70: one `iperf3 -s` serves both, and at 131 ms a finished forward test is still draining the tunnel's smux buffers when the next one dials — which is exactly how the first S2 session lost its last three runs to `the server is busy running a test`. The 400 Mbit/s cap in this file is the one that fits the 131 ms rung it was written for; on the 95.3 ms rung a Go client alone drives 631 Mbit/s, so it BINDS there. The cap belongs to the path, so pass `--bitrate` per session (11.3b ran at 900M) rather than editing this file, and check the workload command line printed beside each result.
